Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as σφαῖρα (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine σφῦρα, a hammer); the ankle (as globular):--ancle bone.
BiblicalUsage: The ankle bones are what gave way and then held. Peter took the lame man by the right hand and lifted him up, and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength. The word names the ankle itself, the joint that had never borne him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ankles are the proof of the healing: the joints that never worked received strength in one moment, and the man walked.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
